8.stimulus: A contraction of "you all," the pronoun "y'all" has long been used as a plural version of "you" in the South and in Black communities around the US. Many varieties of English have no pronoun that specifically addresses more than one person and instead must use "you" to address both one person and more than one. But "y'all" always refers to two or more people. As a result, it conveys the speaker's meaning more precisely than "you" can.

choices.C: Is "y'all" commonly used in English-speaking regions of the world besides the US?
choices.D: Why has the pronoun "y'all" become more widely used in the US?

9.stimulus:
The following text is from Julia Alvarez's 2000 novel In the Name of Salomé. Salomé, a poet, is hosting guests in the front parlor of her family home, and Ramona is her sister. A salon is a social gathering for the exploration of intellectual ideas.

It was evening when the two men got up to leave. Tía Ana had already come into the room several times to see if these guests had departed yet. The front parlor had always been her special province, as she used it for her little school. Now, every evening, it turned into Salomé's salon, as Ramona called it, and it was never in order for its transformation back to a classroom the following morning.

choices.C: She is impatient to share her plans to start a new school with the guests and hopes they will support her.

10.stimulus: Uncle Vanya: Scenes from Country Life in Four Acts is an 1898 play by Anton Chekhov, originally written in Russian. In the play, Professor Serebrakoff and his wife Helena have come to stay at their country estate, which Vanya manages with the help of Sonia, the professor's daughter from a previous marriage. 10.text: Which quotation from a translation of Uncle Vanya most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: Vanya says to himself, "I was proud of [Professor Serebrakoff] and of his learning; I received all his words and writings as inspired and now? Now he has retired, and what is the total of his life? A blank!"
choices.B: Professor Serebrakoff says to Helena, "Ever since I have been old I have been hateful to myself, and I am sure, hateful to you all as well."
choices.C: Professor Serebrakoff says, "I am a book-worm and a scholar, and am unfamiliar with practical affairs. I cannot, I find, dispense with the help of well-informed people."
choices.D: Professor Serebrakoff says to Helena, "I am used to my library and the lecture hall and to the esteem and admiration of my colleagues. Now I suddenly find myself plunged into this wilderness [the estate], condemned to see the same stupid people from morning till night and listen to their futile conversations."

11.stimulus: The Underdogs is a 1915 novel by Mariano Azuela, originally written in Spanish. In the novel, Azuela depicts a traveling group of soldiers as having a renewed sense of agency and authority as they set off on a new stage of their journey: ______
11.text: Which quotation from a translation of The Underdogs most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: "The sonorous, joyful bells rang again. From within the church, the honeyed voices of a female chorus rose melancholy and grave."
choices.B: "All day long [the soldiers] rode through the canyon, up and down the steep, round hills, dirty and bald as a man's head, hill after hill in endless succession. choices.C: "The men threw out their chests as if to breathe the widening horizon, the immensity of the sky, the blue from the mountains and the fresh air, redolent with the various odors of the sierra. They spurred their horses to a gallop as if in that mad race they laid claims of possession to the earth."
choices.D: "Before Juchipila was lost from sight, Valderrama got off his horse, bent down, kneeled, and gravely kissed the ground."

13.stimulus: The Age of Innocence is a 1920 novel by Edith Wharton set in 1870s New York City. In the novel, Newland Archer attends an opera. The narrator describes Newland's tendency to follow the social conventions dictated by other men of New York City society who are in the audience: ______
13.text: Which quotation from The Age of Innocence best illustrates the claim?

choices.A: "Though there was already talk...of a new Opera House which should compete in costliness and splendour with those of the great European capitals, the world of fashion was still content to reassemble every winter in the shabby red and gold boxes of the sociable old Academy [of Music]."
choices.B: "It surprised [Newland] that life should be going on in the old way when his own reactions to it had so completely changed."
choices.C: "Newland Archer felt himself distinctly the superior of these chosen specimens of old New York gentility; he had probably read more, thought more, and even seen a good deal more of the world, than any other man of the number."

24.stimulus:

• Spinach is a vegetable that contains ascorbic acid, an essential nutrient for humans.

25.stimulus:

• Textile researcher Smriti Rai discovered a process for dyeing blue jeans without chemicals.

• Nanocellulose is a natural, plant-based substance that separates the molecules of indigo powder.
25.text: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two approaches to dyeing blue jeans. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.B: Nanocellulose is a natural, plant-based substance that separates the molecules of indigo powder, which doesn't dissolve in water.
choices.C: The traditional approach to dyeing blue jeans is to dip them in a solution containing hazardous chemicals.
choices.D: Rai's approach substitutes a natural, plant-based substance for the hazardous chemicals that manufacturers have traditionally used.

8.stimulus: Optimal foraging theory (OFT) holds that animals' foraging behaviors reflect cost-benefit trade-offs that vary by species and with dynamic ecological circumstances. 8.text: According to the text, the difference between Lang and colleagues' findings and Wright's findings can be attributed to which difference between white-throated round-eared bats and three-striped night monkeys?

choices.A: The bats are less reliant on vision than the monkeys are.
choices.B: The bats decrease their foraging activity as lunar intensity increases, whereas the monkeys increase their foraging activity.
choices.C: The bats are more vulnerable to predators than the monkeys are.

choices.C: Compared with longer-headed dogs, shorter-headed dogs showed less difference in brain activity when hearing either Spanish or Hungarian than when hearing the scrambled recording.
choices.D: Compared with longer-headed dogs, shorter-headed dogs, showed a greater difference in brain activity when hearing the language they were accustomed to than when hearing the other language.

15.stimulus: As complex life cycle parasites, *Opechona* sp. and *Cucullanellus kanabus* require multiple host species throughout their development. Extrapolating from parasite counts on Pacific herring and seven other fish species collected from Puget Sound from 1880 to 2019, Chelsea Wood et al. found that the abundance of three-host parasites, such as *Opechona* sp., negatively correlated with rising average annual sea temperatures; the abundance of two-host parasites, such as *C. kanabus*, was largely stable. Noting that fish and other marine vertebrates are especially vulnerable to climate change, Wood et al. observed that all three-host parasites in the study depend on at least two vertebrate species, while all two-host parasites depend on only one, suggesting that ______
15.text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: although *Opechona* sp. and *C. kanabus* both require Pacific herring as a host, *C. kanabus* was more adversely affected by warming-driven changes in the Pacific herring population than *Opechona* sp. was.
choices.B: a parasite's sensitivity to warming temperatures is negatively correlated with the number of unique vertebrate species it depends on throughout its life cycle.
choices.C: warming-induced population changes among Puget Sound vertebrates may have suppressed some parasite populations, but there were no changes among the eight studied host species that affected two-host parasite abundance.
choices.D: population size and density of the eight fish species examined in the study were likely largely unaffected by rising sea temperatures.

23.stimulus:

• Sculptor Richard Serra of the US won a Carnegie Prize gold medal in 1985.
• Serra's winning artwork was a sculpture entitled *Carnegie*.
23.text: The student wants to contrast the two artworks. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Both *Madame Suggia* and *Carnegie* are Carnegie Prize gold medal-winning artworks.
choices.B: Carnegie Prize gold medals have been awarded to both painters and sculptors.
choices.C: John won a Carnegie Prize gold medal in 1924 for the painting *Madame Suggia*.
choices.D: John's *Madame Suggia* is a painting, while Serra's *Carnegie* is a sculpture.

25.text: The student wants to contrast the number of meteorite falls with the number of meteorite finds. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.B: Meteorites found on Earth are divided into two categories: meteorite falls and meteorite finds.
choices.C: There have been about 1,200 recorded meteorite falls, or meteorites observed falling to Earth.
choices.D: While there have been only about 1,200 recorded meteorite falls, there have been over 60,000 meteorite finds.

choices.B: The Museu de les Ciencies Principe Felipe, which is home to a Foucault pendulum, is in Spain, not Romania.
